payload.name: Extract explicit motivation statements
payload.description: When a message explicitly states what motivates or drives the speaker or their group to improve, use this during extraction to persist the motivating factor as a memory.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly states what motivates or drives them or their group (e.g., 'X pushes us to improve', 'we get better because of X'), create a memory candidate capturing the motivating factor and the behavior it drives.
Prefer a durable memory kind such as state or preference unless the statement describes a single past event; do not skip the message merely because the motivation appears within a larger reply.

solves: The failure was an extraction miss: a message stating what motivates the speaker's group was never captured, leaving later motivation questions unsupported. The mechanism is skipping explicit cause/motivation assertions during extraction. Future inputs where a speaker states what drives them or their group to improve (e.g., 'X drives us to get better') should create a memory. Does not apply to speculative third-party motives or one-off events.
